questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle
questions.problem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(-2i-8j)\,\text{m/s},$ and when $t=4\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $2i\,\text{m/s}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=-2i-8j,\,v=2i,\,t=4,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 2i & =(-2i-8j)+a(4) \\ 4i+8j & =4a \\ a & =\frac{1}{4}(4i+8j) \\  & =(i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Final Velocity of a Particle
questions.problem: The velocity of a particle is $(5i-3j)\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=2\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=5i-3j,\,a=i+2j.
$$

Therefore, after $t=2\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(5i-3j)+(i+2j)(2) \\  & =(5i-3j)+(2i+4j) \\  & =(7i+j)\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Time when a Particle Reaches a Particular Velocity
questions.problem: A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2i-4j)\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}.$ The velocity of the particle is $(-4i+16j)\,\text{ft/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $(8i-8j)\,\text{ft/s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
a=2i-4j,\,u=-4i+16j,\,v=8i-8j
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 8i-8j & =(-4i+16j)+(2i-4j)t \\ 12i-24j & =(2i-4j)t \\ 12i-24j & =2ti-4tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $i$ and $j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}12 & = & 2t \\ -24 & = & -4t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,t=6\,\text{s}.
$$

questions.problem:
A particle moves with constant acceleration. The velocity of the particle equals $(9i-4j)\,\text{km/h}$ both when $t=0\,\text{h}$ and $t=5\,\text{h}.$ What is the acceleration of the particle?

$a=($
{{field-1}}$\,i$
$+$
{{field-2}}$\,j\,)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=9i-4j,\,v=9i-4j,\,t=5
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 9i-4j & =(9i-4j)+a(5) \\ 0 & =5a \\ a & =(0\,i+0\,j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
